issue_context.title: Issue: Object3D `.attach()` emits `added` too early
issue_context.body:
### Description

`.attach(object)` will dispatch "added" event on `object`, but at user-provided event handler, the descendants' world transforms had not been updated, to work around this, users are required to update manually before accessing them

```js
object.addEventListener('added', () => {
  object.updateWorldMatrix(false, true)
```

the workaround is not ideal because threejs anyhow repeats the same after stepout the handler (=update twice):

https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/ce0b3d0415c4bc87a8b4ad01c5d21cc26c6ec5eb/src/core/Object3D.js#L419-L421

review_comments:
Sorry for the late review!

Would you mind undo all changes related to `add()` in this PR? It really should focus on `attach()` and not on other methods. If we change `add()` in this way, we also need to update `remove()` and this is too much for a single PR.

IMO, the optimization for #26740 is not really necessary since `attach()` should be used with objects which are already part of the scene graph. That means they have a parent and thus go through the existing code path and not the new optimized one. In order to keep the method simple as possible, I would leave this bit out for now.
